words.en: An influx of people or things is a large number of them arriving somewhere at the same time.

words.tr: adj. 声音甜美的；悦耳动听的
words.ex: Her mellifluous voice made everyone calm.
words.ex_cn: 她悦耳的声音让每个人都平静下来。
words.en: A mellifluous sound or voice is smooth and pleasant to listen to.

words.ex: The extra words are superfluous.
words.ex_cn: 这些额外的词是多余的。
words.en: Something that is superfluous is unnecessary or no longer needed.

words.ex: The price of oil fluctuates every day.
words.ex_cn: 油价每天都在波动。
words.en: To fluctuate means to change or vary frequently and unpredictably.

words.ex: My forebear came from Ireland long ago.
words.ex_cn: 我的祖先很久以前来自爱尔兰。
words.en: Your forebears are your ancestors, especially your grandparents or earlier relatives.

words.ex: A sense of foreboding filled the room as the storm approached.
words.ex_cn: 随着暴风雨的临近，房间里充满了不祥的预感。
words.en: A foreboding is a feeling that something bad is going to happen.

words.ex: I cannot foresee what will happen tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 我无法预知明天会发生什么。
words.en: If you foresee something, you expect and believe that it will happen.

words.tr: v. 预先阻止；抢先一步
words.ex: He forestalls problems by planning ahead.
words.ex_cn: 他通过提前计划来防止问题。
words.en: To forestall something means to prevent it from happening or to act before someone else does in order to prevent them from doing something.

words.ex: The heat made the metal deform.
words.ex_cn: 热量使金属变形。
words.en: To deform something means to change its shape, usually in a way that makes it less attractive or useful.

words.ex: The new teacher transformed the class into a lively group.
words.ex_cn: 这位新老师把班级变成了一个充满活力的团体。
words.en: To transform something or someone means to change them completely and usually improve their appearance, form, or structure.

words.ex: The visa application requires a lot of formality.
words.ex_cn: 签证申请需要很多正式手续。
words.en: A formality is something that is done as part of a formal process or procedure, often without much thought or feeling because it is expected.

words.ex: The teacher gave us important information about the test.
words.ex_cn: 老师给了我们关于考试的重要信息。
words.en: Information is facts or details about a subject, event, or situation.

words.ex: The teacher will formulate a new rule for class.
words.ex_cn: 老师将制定一条新的课堂规则。
words.en: If you formulate something such as a plan or proposal, you invent it, thinking about the details carefully.

words.ex: He conform to the rules of the school.
words.ex_cn: 他遵守学校的规章制度。
words.en: To conform means to behave in a way that is accepted by most people or to obey a rule, law, or custom.

words.tr:
n. 顺从者；随波逐流者；循规蹈矩的人
adj. 墨守成规的
words.ex: He is a conformist who always follows the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是遵守规则的顺从者。
words.en: A conformist is someone who behaves in the same way as most other people in a society or group, especially because they do not want to be different or because they want to be accepted by other people.

words.ex: His performance in the game was excellent.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中的表现非常出色。
words.en: The act of performing a play, concert, or some other form of entertainment.

words.ex: She made the dance look effortless.
words.ex_cn: 她让舞蹈看起来毫不费力。
words.en: If you describe something as effortless, you mean that it is done or achieved with very little difficulty or work, often as a result of great skill.

words.tr: v. 设防御工事；加强；增加营养物
words.ex: The soldiers fortify the hill with walls and trenches.
words.ex_cn: 士兵们在山上用墙壁和战壕设防御工事。
words.en: To strengthen a place with defensive works so as to protect it against attack; to strengthen or invigorate someone mentally or physically.

words.ex: He showed great fortitude during the hard times.
words.ex_cn: 他在艰难时期展现了极大的毅力。
words.en: Fortitude is the mental and emotional strength that enables a person to face difficulty, danger, or pain without fear.

words.ex: He was forcibly taken by the police.
words.ex_cn: 他被警察强行带走了。
words.en: In a way that involves physical force or strength, especially against someone's will.

words.ex: The police enforce the law.
words.ex_cn: 警察强制执行法律。
words.en: If people in authority enforce a law or a rule, they make sure that it is obeyed, usually by punishing people who do not obey it.

words.ex: Exercise can reinforce your muscles.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的肌肉。
words.en: To reinforce something means to make it stronger or more effective.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；难驾驭的；脾气不好的
words.ex: The fractious child refused to eat his vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 这个脾气暴躁的孩子拒绝吃蔬菜。
words.en: If you describe someone as fractious, you mean they are easily upset or annoyed, and often complain.

words.ex: He fractured his arm during the soccer game.
words.ex_cn: 他在足球比赛中摔断了手臂。
words.en: If something such as a bone fractures or is fractured, it breaks or cracks.

words.tr: adj. 执拗的；难驾驭的；难以治愈的
words.ex: The refractory material can withstand high temperatures.
words.ex_cn: 这种耐火材料能承受高温。
words.en: Stubbornly resistant to authority or control; difficult to melt or work; resistant to heat.

words.ex: He got a fine for a small infraction.
words.ex_cn: 他因一个小违规行为被罚款。
words.en: An infraction is a violation or infringement of a law, agreement, or set of rules.

words.ex: The town is near the frontier of the country.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇靠近国家的边境。
words.en: A frontier is a border between two countries or the area close to it. It can also refer to the limit of knowledge or the most advanced or recent stage in the development of something.

words.ex: You need to pay the upfront fee before the service starts.
words.ex_cn: 你需要在服务开始前支付预付款。
words.en: If you are upfront about something, you are honest and open about it.

words.tr:
n. （当众）侮辱；冒犯
v. （当众）侮辱；冒犯
words.ex: He felt an affront when they laughed at his idea.
words.ex_cn: 当他们嘲笑他的想法时，他感到受到了冒犯。
words.en: If something is an affront to you, it is an action or remark that insults or offends you.

words.ex: He must confront his fears.
words.ex_cn: 他必须面对自己的恐惧。
words.en: If you confront a difficult situation or issue, you accept the fact that it exists and try to deal with it.

words.ex: He had the effrontery to lie to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他竟敢对老师撒谎。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as effrontery, you are emphasizing that it is very rude or disrespectful.

words.tr: adj. 功能的；起作用的；实用的；
words.ex: This chair is functional and comfortable.
words.ex_cn: 这把椅子功能性强且舒适。
words.en: Relating to the way in which something works or operates.

words.ex: The functionary's job is to ensure that the procedures are followed correctly.
words.ex_cn: 这位公职人员的工作是确保程序正确执行。
words.en: A functionary is a person who has to perform official functions or duties; an official.

words.tr: adj. 功能失调的；出现障碍的；
words.ex: The dysfunctional family rarely ate meals together.
words.ex_cn: 这个功能失调的家庭很少一起吃饭。
words.en: Not operating normally or properly.

words.ex: The car had a malfunction in the engine.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的发动机出现了故障。
words.en: If a machine or device malfunctions, it fails to work properly.

words.ex: He gave a perfunctory nod and left.
words.ex_cn: 他敷衍地点了点头，然后离开了。
words.en: If you describe something that is done as perfunctory, you mean that it is done as a duty or a formality, without much care or interest.

words.tr: v. 弥漫于；充满；扩散；布满
words.ex: The sunset suffuses the sky with orange light.
words.ex_cn: 日落将天空染成橙色。
words.en: If something such as a colour, emotion, or light suffuses a person or thing, it gradually spreads over or through them.

words.tr:
v. 弥漫；
adj. 分散的；
words.ex: Smoke began to diffuse through the room.
words.ex_cn: 烟开始弥漫在整个房间里。
words.en: If something such as knowledge or information is diffused, or if it diffuses, it is made known over a wide area or to a lot of people.

words.tr: adj. 溢于言表的；感情奔放的
words.ex: She was effusive in her praise for the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 她对老师的赞美非常热情。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as effusive, you mean that they express pleasure, gratitude, or approval in a very enthusiastic way.

words.ex: The teacher tried to infuse confidence into the students.
words.ex_cn: 老师试图向学生注入信心。
words.en: If you infuse a quality into someone or something, you fill them with it. If a quality infuses something, it is present throughout it.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；不吝惜的；浪费的
words.ex: He was profuse in thanks after the rescue.
words.ex_cn: 获救后，他表达了深深的感谢。
words.en: If you describe something as profuse, you mean that it is very plentiful or abundant.

words.ex: The police helped to defuse the situation.
words.ex_cn: 警察帮助减少了危险。
words.en: To remove the fuse from (an explosive device) in order to prevent it from exploding; to reduce the danger or tension in (a situation).

words.tr: n. 概论；普遍性；一般性；通则
words.ex: The book gives a generality of modern physics.
words.ex_cn: 这本书对现代物理学做了概论。
words.en: A generality is a statement that is very general and not specific, often used when the speaker does not want to give details or when the details are not known.

words.ex: He made a generalization from the data.
words.ex_cn: 他从数据中做出了一个概括。
words.en: A generalization is a statement that seems to be true in most situations or for most people, but that may not be completely true in all cases.

words.ex: He bought a generic brand of painkiller.
words.ex_cn: 他买了一种普通的止痛药品牌。
words.en: Generic refers to something that is not specific or unique, often used to describe products that are not branded or are general in nature.

words.tr: adj. 亲切的；和蔼的；温暖的
words.ex: He is a genial man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Friendly and cheerful.

words.ex: The weather was congenial for a picnic.
words.ex_cn: 天气非常适合野餐。
words.en: A congenial person, place, or environment is pleasant because it suits your character or nature.

words.ex: My generation grew up with smartphones.
words.ex_cn: 我们这一代人是伴随着智能手机长大的。
words.en: A generation is all the people in a group or country who are of a similar age, especially when they are considered as having the same experiences or attitudes.

words.ex: The generator provides electricity during the power outage.
words.ex_cn: 发电机在停电时提供电力。
words.en: A generator is a machine which produces electricity or another form of energy.

words.ex: Poverty can engender crime.
words.ex_cn: 贫困会引起犯罪。
words.en: To cause a feeling, situation, or condition to exist.

words.ex: Lizards can regenerate their tails.
words.ex_cn: 蜥蜴可以再生尾巴。
words.en: To regenerate means to grow or form again, especially after being damaged or lost, or to improve a place or system by making it more active or successful.

words.tr:
adj. 退步的；堕落的；腐化的
v. 退化；堕落
n. 堕落的人
words.ex: The old machine became degenerate and stopped working.
words.ex_cn: 这台旧机器退步了，停止工作了。
words.en: If you say that someone or something degenerates, you mean that they become worse in some way, for example, poorer, weaker, or less respectable.

words.tr: adj. 无知的；缺乏知识的
words.ex: He was ignorant of the basic rules.
words.ex_cn: 他对基本规则一无所知。
words.en: If you describe someone as ignorant, you mean that they do not know things they should know. If someone is ignorant of a fact, they do not know it.

words.tr:
n. 不可知论者
adj. 不可知论的
words.ex: He is agnostic about religion.
words.ex_cn: 他对宗教持不可知论态度。
words.en: An agnostic is someone who believes that it is not possible to know whether God exists or not.

words.ex: The doctor can diagnose the illness quickly.
words.ex_cn: 医生能很快诊断出这种病。
words.en: If someone or something is diagnosed as having a particular illness or problem, their illness or problem is identified. If an illness or problem is diagnosed, it is identified.

words.tr:
adj. 倒退的；退化的；退步的
v. 逆行；倒退；堕落
words.ex: The company's retrograde policies led to a decline in productivity.
words.ex_cn: 公司倒退的政策导致了生产力的下降。
words.en: If you describe an action or idea as retrograde, you disapprove of it because it returns to old ideas or methods and does not take advantage of recent progress.

words.tr:
v. 使降低；使降级
n. 下坡路
words.ex: The company decided to downgrade the software version.
words.ex_cn: 公司决定将软件版本降级。
words.en: To downgrade something means to reduce its quality, value, or status.

words.tr: adj. 低级的；品质低劣的
words.ex: The company produces low-grade products that are not durable.
words.ex_cn: 该公司生产的产品质量低劣，不耐用。
words.en: Of inferior quality or value.

words.tr: adj. 逐渐的；逐步的；渐进的；
words.ex: The change was gradual.
words.ex_cn: 这种变化是逐渐的。
words.en: A gradual change or process happens in small stages over a long period of time, rather than suddenly.

words.ex: The grandeur of the palace amazed everyone.
words.ex_cn: 宫殿的宏伟让每个人都感到惊讶。
words.en: The quality of being grand or splendid in appearance or style.

words.ex: The palace has a grandiose design with tall columns and golden domes.
words.ex_cn: 这座宫殿有着宏伟的设计，配有高大的柱子和金色的圆顶。
words.en: If you describe something as grandiose, you mean it is larger or more elaborate than necessary, or it is intended to seem very impressive or magnificent.

words.tr: adj. 词藻浮华的；夸大的；做作的
words.ex: He gave a grandiloquent speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's language as grandiloquent, you mean that it is extremely formal, elaborate, or exaggerated, and is used to impress people.

words.ex: He tries to aggrandize himself by lying about his achievements.
words.ex_cn: 他通过吹嘘自己的成就来抬高自己。
words.en: To increase the power, status, or wealth of someone or something.

words.ex: He gratifies his parents by getting good grades.
words.ex_cn: 他通过取得好成绩来让父母感到欣慰。
words.en: If you are gratified by something, it gives you pleasure or satisfaction.

words.ex: He showed gratitude for the help.
words.ex_cn: 他表达了对帮助的感激。
words.en: Gratitude is the feeling of being thankful and appreciative.

words.tr:
adj. 免费的；无偿的
adv. 免费地；无偿地
words.ex: You can download the software gratis from the company's website.
words.ex_cn: 你可以从公司网站免费下载该软件。
words.en: If something is done or given gratis, it is done or given without payment.

words.tr: n. 小费；赏钱；退职金；退伍金
words.ex: She left a small gratuity on the table for the waiter.
words.ex_cn: 她在桌上给服务员留下了一点小费。
words.en: A gratuity is a sum of money given to someone, typically to a service worker, in addition to the payment due for the service provided.

words.tr: adj. 无故的；无必要的；无偿的；免费的
words.ex: He made a gratuitous comment about her clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的衣服做了毫无必要的评论。
words.en: If you describe something as gratuitous, you mean that it is unnecessary, and often harmful or upsetting.

words.tr:
n. 总计；集合体
adj. 合计的；总的
v. （使）聚集；聚合；总计为
words.ex: The aggregate of all sales this month is $50,000.
words.ex_cn: 本月所有销售额的总计是5万美元。
words.en: An aggregate is a number of things or people that are considered as a group or a whole.

words.ex: People congregate in the park on weekends.
words.ex_cn: 人们在周末聚集在公园里。
words.en: To congregate means to come together in a group or crowd.

words.ex: Dolphins are gregarious animals that swim in groups.
words.ex_cn: 海豚是群居动物，成群游泳。
words.en: Someone who is gregarious enjoys being with other people.

words.tr: adj. 攻击性的；有进取心的；侵略性的；
words.ex: The dog showed aggressive behavior toward strangers.
words.ex_cn: 这只狗对陌生人表现出攻击性行为。
words.en: An aggressive person or animal has a quality of anger and determination that makes them ready to attack others.

words.ex: He digresses when he talks about his vacation.
words.ex_cn: 他谈论假期时会跑题。
words.en: If you digress, you move away from the subject you are talking or writing about and talk or write about something different for a while.

words.ex: This school uses a progressive teaching method.
words.ex_cn: 这所学校使用一种先进的教学方法。
words.en: A progressive person or idea is one that is modern and new, and is interested in change and improvement.

words.tr: adj. 退化的；倒退的；回归的
words.ex: The patient's condition showed a regressive trend after the surgery.
words.ex_cn: 手术后，病人的情况显示出退化的趋势。
words.en: A regressive action, process, or idea is one that involves returning to an earlier and less advanced stage of development.

words.ex: He was punished for transgressing the law.
words.ex_cn: 他因违法而受到惩罚。
words.en: To transgress means to go beyond the limits of what is morally, socially, or legally acceptable.

words.ex: The only egress from the building was blocked by debris.
words.ex_cn: 建筑物的唯一出口被碎片堵住了。
words.en: Egress refers to the act of going out or exiting from a place.

words.tr: adj. 适合居住的；可居住的；
words.ex: The planet is habitable because it has water and air.
words.ex_cn: 这颗行星有水和空气，适合居住。
words.en: A place that is habitable is suitable or good enough for people to live in.

words.ex: Parents habituate children to eat vegetables early.
words.ex_cn: 父母从小就让孩子习惯吃蔬菜。
words.en: To make or become used to something as a result of repeated exposure.

words.tr: adj. 惯常的；习惯性的；经常的；
words.ex: He is a habitual smoker.
words.ex_cn: 他是个惯常的吸烟者。
words.en: A habitual action, state, or way of behaving is one that someone usually does or has, especially one that is considered to be typical or characteristic of them.

words.tr: n. 栖息地；居留地；产地；
words.ex: The panda's habitat is in the mountains of China.
words.ex_cn: 熊猫的栖息地在中国的山区。
words.en: The natural environment in which a species or group of species lives.

words.ex: They cohabit in a small apartment.
words.ex_cn: 他们同住在一个小公寓里。
words.en: To live together and have a sexual relationship without being married.

words.tr: v. 恢复；修复；改造（罪犯）
words.ex: The hospital will rehabilitate the injured athlete.
words.ex_cn: 医院将帮助受伤的运动员康复。
words.en: To rehabilitate someone who has been ill or in prison means to help them to live a normal life again. To rehabilitate a building or an area means to improve its condition.

words.tr: adv. 方便地；轻易地；便利地
words.ex: She won the game handily.
words.ex_cn: 她轻松地赢得了比赛。
words.en: In a manner that is easy to use or manage; with skill or dexterity.

words.tr:
v. 处理；操纵；
n. 把手；柄；
words.ex: He can handle difficult problems easily.
words.ex_cn: 他能轻松处理难题。
words.en: To deal with or control a situation or problem.

words.tr:
n. 手铐；思想上的桎梏
v. 用手铐铐住（某人）；把（某人）铐在（某物、某人）上；限制
words.ex: The police put handcuff on the thief.
words.ex_cn: 警察给小偷戴上了手铐。
words.en: A handcuff is a pair of lockable linked metal rings for securing a prisoner's wrists.

words.ex: They shook hands with a firm handshake.
words.ex_cn: 他们以坚定的握手示意友好。
words.en: A handshake is a gesture in which two people grasp one of each other's like hands, in most cases accompanied by a brief up and down movement of the grasped hands.

words.ex: His handwriting is very neat.
words.ex_cn: 他的笔迹非常工整。
words.en: Handwriting is the style of writing that someone uses when they write with a pen or pencil.

words.tr:
adj. 即时的；未经准备的；唐突无礼的
adv. 即时地；未经思索地；随便地
words.ex: He gave an offhand answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个即时的回答。
words.en: If you say something offhand, you say it without checking the details or facts of it beforehand.

words.ex: The hapless boy lost his wallet and got caught in the rain.
words.ex_cn: 这个倒霉的男孩丢了钱包，还被雨淋了。
words.en: If you describe someone as hapless, you mean that they are unlucky or unfortunate.

words.tr: n. 不幸之事；灾祸；恶运
words.ex: He had a little mishap when he dropped his coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心把咖啡洒了，出了点小差错。
words.en: A mishap is an unlucky accident.

words.ex: He arranged the books in a haphazard way.
words.ex_cn: 他随意地摆放了书。
words.en: If you describe something as haphazard, you are critical of it because it is not at all organized or is not arranged according to a plan.

words.tr: v. 朝向；前进；“head”的现在分词； n. 标题；
words.ex: The ship is heading north.
words.ex_cn: 船正朝北航行。
words.en: A heading is a word, phrase, or sentence at the beginning of a written passage that explains what it's about.

words.tr: adj. 刚愎自用的；顽固的；任性的
words.ex: He is headstrong and refuses to listen.
words.ex_cn: 他很固执，不肯听别人的话。
words.en: If you refer to someone as headstrong, you are slightly critical of them because they are very determined to do what they want, and refuse to be advised by others.

words.tr: adj. 易怒的；性急的；易激动的
words.ex: He was too hotheaded to make a good leader.
words.ex_cn: 他太性急了，不适合做领导。
words.en: If you describe someone as hotheaded, you are criticizing them for acting too quickly, without thinking of the consequences.

words.tr: n. 装饰船头的人像；傀儡领袖；有名无实的首脑；
words.ex: The old ship had a wooden figurehead of a lion.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船的船头有一个木制的狮子像。
words.en: A figurehead is a person who is the head of an organization or country in name only, without any real power or authority.

words.ex: She gave a heartfelt thank you to her teacher.
words.ex_cn: 她向老师真诚地表达了感谢。
words.en: If you describe something such as a feeling or emotion as heartfelt, you mean that it is genuine and strongly felt.

words.ex: His heartiness in helping others was evident to everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他对帮助他人的热心对每个人来说都是显而易见的。
words.en: The quality of being hearty; enthusiasm, warmth, or sincerity.

words.ex: He is too faint-hearted to speak in front of the class.
words.ex_cn: 他太胆小了，不敢在全班面前说话。
words.en: Lacking courage or determination; timid.

words.tr: adj. 轻松愉快的；无忧无虑的；随便的；漫不经心的
words.ex: He gave a lighthearted laugh during the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上开心地笑了。
words.en: If someone is lighthearted, they are cheerful and happy.

words.ex: He was stouthearted and faced the storm.
words.ex_cn: 他勇敢地面对了风暴。
words.en: Having or showing courage and determination.

words.ex: Her smile heartened the tired students.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑鼓舞了疲惫的学生。
words.en: If someone is heartened by something, it encourages them and makes them cheerful.

words.tr:
n.  水合物；氢氧化物
v. （使）成水合物
words.ex: The crystal is a hydrate of copper sulfate.
words.ex_cn: 这种晶体是硫酸铜的水合物。
words.en: To hydrate means to cause something to absorb water or to supply water or liquid to someone or something in order to maintain healthy bodily functions. It can also refer to a compound, typically a crystalline one, in which water molecules are chemically bound to another compound or an element.

words.ex: The sun can dehydrate your skin quickly.
words.ex_cn: 太阳会很快使你的皮肤脱水。
words.en: To dehydrate something means to remove all the water from it, often in order to preserve it. If you dehydrate, you lose too much water from your body, usually because of illness or extreme heat.

words.ex: Bread and rice are rich in carbohydrate.
words.ex_cn: 面包和米饭富含碳水化合物。
words.en: A carbohydrate is a substance found in foods such as bread, potatoes, and rice which provides your body with heat and energy and which consists of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen.

words.tr: n. 活动过度；极度活跃
words.ex: The child shows hyperactivity during class.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子在课堂上表现出多动。
words.en: Hyperactivity is a state of being unusually or abnormally active.

words.ex: He uses hyperbole when he says he is dying of hunger.
words.ex_cn: 当他说到自己快饿死了时，他用了夸张的说法。
words.en: Hyperbole is a way of speaking or writing that makes someone or something sound bigger, better, more, etc. than they are.

words.tr: adj. 苛求的；吹毛求疵的
words.ex: He is hypercritical about small mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他对小错误非常吹毛求疵。
words.en: If you say that someone is hypercritical, you mean that they criticize things too much or too severely.

words.ex: He is hypocritical when he says he hates lying but lies all the time.
words.ex_cn: 他说他讨厌撒谎，却总是撒谎，这很虚伪。
words.en: If you accuse someone of being hypocritical, you mean that they pretend to have qualities, beliefs, or feelings that they do not really have.

words.ex: He is a hypocrite because he says he loves peace but fights often.
words.ex_cn: 他是个伪君子，因为他声称热爱和平，却经常打架。
words.en: A hypocrite is someone who pretends to have certain beliefs or opinions that they do not really have, especially in order to deceive people.

words.tr: n. 疑病症; 忧郁症，疑病症，季肋部( hypochondrium的名词复数 )
words.ex: Her hypochondria led her to visit the doctor frequently.
words.ex_cn: 她的疑病症使她频繁地去看医生。
words.en: Hypochondria is a condition in which a person is excessively and unduly worried about having a serious illness.

words.ex: He made a hypothesis that plants grow faster in light.
words.ex_cn: 他提出一个假设，认为植物在光照下长得更快。
words.en: A hypothesis is an idea which is suggested as a possible explanation for a particular situation or condition, but which has not yet been proved to be correct.

words.ex: He has dyslexia, so he reads slowly.
words.ex_cn: 他有阅读障碍，所以读得慢。
words.en: Dyslexia is a learning difficulty that primarily affects the skills involved in accurate and fluent word reading and spelling.

words.ex: He has amnesia and cannot remember his name.
words.ex_cn: 他患有失忆症，想不起自己的名字。
words.en: Amnesia is a medical condition that affects someone's memory and they are unable to remember events or information.

words.ex: He feels weak because he has anemia.
words.ex_cn: 他感到虚弱，因为他患有贫血。
words.en: A condition in which there is a deficiency of red cells or of haemoglobin in the blood, resulting in pallor and weariness.

words.ex: Hemophilia is a genetic disorder that impairs the body's ability to make blood clots.
words.ex_cn: 血友病是一种遗传性疾病，会损害身体形成血块的能力。
words.en: A hereditary disorder where the blood does not clot properly, leading to excessive bleeding.

words.ex: The crowd fell into hysteria when the fire alarm sounded.
words.ex_cn: 当火警响起时，人群陷入了情绪失控。
words.en: Hysteria is a state of extreme excitement, fear, or anger in which people cannot control their emotions or behavior.

words.ex: He has insomnia and cannot sleep at night.
words.ex_cn: 他有失眠症，晚上睡不着。
words.en: If someone suffers from insomnia, they find it difficult to sleep.

words.tr: n. 狂热； 癖好；躁狂症
words.ex: He has a mania for collecting stamps.
words.ex_cn: 他痴迷于收集邮票。
words.en: An extreme enthusiasm or desire for something, often to the point of obsession.

words.ex: He felt nostalgia when he saw his old toy.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到自己的旧玩具时，感到怀旧。
words.en: A sentimental longing or wistful affection for the past, typically for a period or place with happy personal associations.

words.ex: His paranoia made him believe that everyone was out to get him.
words.ex_cn: 他的多疑让他相信每个人都在算计他。
words.en: Paranoia is the unreasonable feeling that you are being threatened in some way, or that people are trying to harm you, without any evidence.

words.ex: Doctors must follow medical ethics.
words.ex_cn: 医生必须遵守医学道德规范。
words.en: Ethics are moral beliefs and rules about right and wrong.

words.ex: He is learning genetics in biology class.
words.ex_cn: 他在生物课上学习遗传学。
words.en: Genetics is the study of how characteristics are passed from one generation to another through genes.

words.ex: He is studying linguistics at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学学习语言学。
words.en: Linguistics is the scientific study of language and its structure, including the study of morphology, syntax, phonetics, and semantics.

words.ex: He is interested in metaphysics and asks big questions about life.
words.ex_cn: 他对形而上学感兴趣，会思考关于生命的重大问题。
words.en: Metaphysics is a branch of philosophy that deals with the first principles of things, including abstract concepts such as being, knowing, substance, cause, identity, time, and space.

words.ex: He uses mnemonics to remember the dates.
words.ex_cn: 他使用助记法来记住这些日期。
words.en: Mnemonics is a method or system for improving the memory by using formulas or techniques.

words.tr: v. 隔离；使隔热；使隔音；使绝缘
words.ex: The walls insulate the house from cold air.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁将房子与冷空气隔离开。
words.en: To insulate something means to protect it from heat, cold, noise, or electricity by covering it in a material that prevents it from passing through.

words.ex: The insularity of Japan affects its cultural traditions.
words.ex_cn: 日本的岛国特性影响了它的文化传统。
words.en: The state of being isolated or detached from others, often resulting in a narrow or limited perspective.

words.ex: He takes insulin to control his blood sugar.
words.ex_cn: 他注射胰岛素来控制血糖。
words.en: A hormone produced in the pancreas by the islets of Langerhans, which regulates the amount of glucose in the blood. The lack of insulin causes a form of diabetes.

words.ex: The peninsula is surrounded by water on three sides.
words.ex_cn: 这个半岛三面环水。
words.en: A peninsula is a piece of land that is almost entirely surrounded by water but is connected to the mainland on one side.

words.ex: He tried to integrate into the new school community.
words.ex_cn: 他试图融入新的学校群体。
words.en: If someone integrates into a social group, or is integrated into it, they behave in such a way that they become part of the group or are accepted into it.

words.ex: The old bridge will disintegrate if no one fixes it.
words.ex_cn: 如果没人修理，这座旧桥会瓦解。
words.en: If something disintegrates, it breaks into many small pieces or parts and is destroyed.

words.ex: Honesty is an integral part of a good relationship.
words.ex_cn: 诚实是良好关系中不可或缺的一部分。
words.en: Something that is integral is very important or necessary. If something is an integral part of a whole, it is an essential part of that whole.

words.ex: He lost his job because of his integrity.
words.ex_cn: 他因为正直而失去了工作。
words.en: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

words.ex: There is a five-minute interval between the two classes.
words.ex_cn: 两节课之间有五分钟的间隔。
words.en: An interval is a period of time between two events or dates.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；间歇的
words.ex: The rain is intermittent today.
words.ex_cn: 今天雨断断续续地下。
words.en: Something that is intermittent happens occasionally rather than continuously.

words.tr: n. 间歇；暂停；中间休息
words.ex: There is a ten-minute intermission during the play.
words.ex_cn: 这场戏中间有十分钟的中场休息。
words.en: An intermission is a short break between parts of a play, film, concert, or other performance.

words.ex: He interrupted me while I was speaking.
words.ex_cn: 我在说话时他打断了我。
words.en: To interrupt someone means to stop them from speaking by saying or doing something, or to cause something to stop happening for a period of time.

words.ex: He will intercede for his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他会为他的朋友出面说情。
words.en: If you intercede with someone, you try to persuade them to forgive someone or end their disagreement with them.

words.ex: Don't interfere when I am working.
words.ex_cn: 我工作时不要打扰。
words.en: To interfere means to involve oneself in a situation where one is not wanted or needed, often causing problems or hindering progress.

words.tr: adj. 暂时的；临时的；期间的；
words.ex: He is the interim manager until a new one is hired.
words.ex_cn: 在招聘到新的经理之前，他是临时经理。
words.en: An interim is a period of time between one event, process, or period and another, especially one of temporary nature.

words.ex: He interjected during the meeting to ask a question.
words.ex_cn: 他在会议中插话问了一个问题。
words.en: To say something that interrupts someone who is speaking.

words.tr: n. 闯入者；干涉他人事务者
words.ex: The interloper walked into the meeting without permission.
words.ex_cn: 那个闯入者未经允许走进了会议。
words.en: An interloper is someone who becomes involved in a situation or place where they are not wanted or are considered not to belong.

words.ex: The historian interpolated the text with his own opinions.
words.ex_cn: 这位历史学家在文本中插入了自己的观点。
words.en: To interpolate means to insert something between other things or parts, especially to insert words into a text.

words.ex: She intersperses flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 她在花园里分散地种着花。
words.en: To place something at intervals among other things.

words.ex: His judgment was clear and fair.
words.ex_cn: 他的判断清晰而公正。
words.en: A judgment is an opinion that you have or express after thinking carefully about something.

words.tr: adj. 司法的；法庭的；审判的；
words.ex: The judicial system protects people's rights.
words.ex_cn: 司法系统保护人民的权利。
words.en: Judicial means relating to the legal system and to judgments made in a court of law.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有见识的；判断正确的
words.ex: He made a judicious choice about which book to buy.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个明智的买书决定。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as judicious, you approve of it because you think that it shows good judgment and sense.

words.ex: The judge will adjudicate the dispute next week.
words.ex_cn: 法官将在下周裁决这场纠纷。
words.en: To adjudicate means to make an official decision about a problem or dispute.

words.ex: He has prejudice against people from other countries.
words.ex_cn: 他对来自其他国家的人有偏见。
words.en: Prejudice is an unreasonable dislike of a particular group of people or things, or a preference for one group of people or things over another.

words.ex: The jury decided the man was innocent.
words.ex_cn: 陪审团裁定这个人无罪。
words.en: A jury is a group of people who are chosen to decide whether someone is guilty or not guilty of a crime in a court of law.

words.tr: n. 法学家；法律学专家
words.ex: The jurist provided a detailed analysis of the legal case.
words.ex_cn: 法学家对这起法律案件进行了详细的分析。
words.en: A jurist is someone who is an expert in law, especially one who gives advice on legal matters or writes about law.

words.ex: He was charged with perjury after lying in court.
words.ex_cn: 他在法庭上撒谎后被控伪证罪。
words.en: The crime of telling a lie in a court of law after having sworn to tell the truth.

words.tr: v. 公开放弃；发誓断绝
words.ex: He had to abjure his old beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不放弃他的旧信仰。
words.en: If you abjure something such as a belief or way of life, you state publicly that you will give it up or that you reject it.

words.ex: The wizard conjure a fireball with ancient words.
words.ex_cn: 巫师用古老的咒语召唤出一个火球。
words.en: If you conjure something out of nothing, you make it appear as if by magic.

words.tr:
adj. 缓慢而困难的；费力的；不自然的
v. 努力；干苦力活；“labor”的过去式和过去分词
words.ex: His speech was labored and hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的演讲吃力且难以理解。
words.en: If something is labored, it is done with great difficulty and effort, often in a way that seems unnatural or forced.

words.ex: The laborer works hard every day.
words.ex_cn: 这名工人每天努力工作。
words.en: A laborer is a person who does unskilled physical work, especially outdoors.

words.ex: He works in a laboratory on Fridays.
words.ex_cn: 他在星期五去实验室工作。
words.en: A laboratory is a place equipped for scientific research, experiments, or teaching.

words.ex: Cleaning the whole house is a laborious task.
words.ex_cn: 打扫整个房子是一项耗时费力的任务。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as laborious, you mean that it takes a lot of time and effort.

words.tr: v. 痛击；痛斥；冗长地解释
words.ex: He belabored the point until everyone was bored.
words.ex_cn: 他反复讨论那个观点，直到大家都感到厌烦。
words.en: To argue or discuss (a subject) in excessive detail; to attack or criticize (someone) persistently.

words.ex: They collaborate to finish the project.
words.ex_cn: 他们合作完成这个项目。
words.en: to work jointly with others or together especially in an intellectual endeavor

words.tr:
adj. 精心制作的；详尽的；
v. 精心制作；详尽阐述；
words.ex: She wore an elaborate dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件精心制作的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: To elaborate means to add more details to something that has already been said or written, making it more complex or detailed. As an adjective, it describes something that is very complex and detailed.

words.ex: The landlord fixed the broken window.
words.ex_cn: 房东修好了破掉的窗户。
words.en: A landlord is a person who owns land or property and rents it out to others.

words.ex: The invention of the wheel was a landmark in human history.
words.ex_cn: 轮子的发明是人类历史上的一个里程碑。
words.en: A landmark is a building or feature of a landscape that is easily seen and recognized from a distance, especially one that enables someone to establish their location.

words.ex: The landscape after the rain is very beautiful.
words.ex_cn: 雨后的景色非常美丽。
words.en: A landscape is all the visible features of an area of land, often considered in terms of their aesthetic appeal.

words.tr: n. 山崩；塌方；压倒性的胜利
words.ex: The heavy rain caused a landslide.
words.ex_cn: 大雨引发了山体滑坡。
words.en: A landslide is a victory in an election in which a person or political party gets far more votes or seats than their opponents.

words.ex: He lives on a small island.
words.ex_cn: 他住在一个小岛上。
words.en: An island is a piece of land that is completely surrounded by water.

words.ex: The old factory became a wasteland after it closed.
words.ex_cn: 工厂关闭后，它变成了一片荒地。
words.en: A wasteland is an area of land that is uncultivated or uninhabited, often because it is barren or devastated.

words.tr: adj. 松弛的；懒散的；马虎的
words.ex: He is lax about his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对作业很松懈。
words.en: If you say that a person's behaviour or a system is lax, you mean they are not careful or strict about maintaining high standards.

words.tr:
adj. 通便的
n. 泻药；通便剂
words.ex: The doctor prescribed a laxative for his constipation.
words.ex_cn: 医生给他开了一种泻药来治疗便秘。
words.en: A laxative is a substance that you take to make you go to the toilet, especially when you are constipated.

words.ex: He listens to music to relax.
words.ex_cn: 他听音乐来放松。
words.en: If you relax or if something relaxes you, you feel more calm and less worried or tense.

words.ex: The accident caused paralysis in his legs.
words.ex_cn: 这次事故导致他双腿瘫痪。
words.en: Paralysis is the loss of the ability to move and sometimes to feel anything in part or most of the body, typically as a result of illness, poison, or injury.

words.ex: His collection of old coins is very rare.
words.ex_cn: 他收集的旧硬币非常稀有。
words.en: A collection is a group of things, often of the same type, that have been gathered together over a period of time.

words.tr:
adj. 集体的；
n. 集体；
words.ex: The collective decision was made by all members.
words.ex_cn: 这个集体决定是由所有成员做出的。
words.en: done or shared by all members of a group of people

words.ex: The election will be held next month.
words.ex_cn: 选举将在下个月举行。
words.en: An election is a process in which people vote to choose a person or group of people to hold an official position.

words.tr:
adj. 选举的；选修的；可选择的
n. 选修课程
words.ex: He voted in the elective process for mayor.
words.ex_cn: 他参加了市长的选举过程。
words.en: An elective course or subject is one that you can choose to study as part of your course, rather than one that you have to study.

words.tr:
adj. 不拘一格的；兼收并蓄的；折中的
n. 折中主义者
words.ex: He has an eclectic taste in music.
words.ex_cn: 他对音乐的品味很广泛多样。
words.en: An eclectic collection or group is a wide range of different things or people.

words.tr: adj. 选择性的；精挑细选的；
words.ex: He is selective about what he eats.
words.ex_cn: 他对吃的东西很挑剔。
words.en: If you are selective, you choose things carefully, for example, the things that you buy or do.

words.tr: n. （教堂中的）诵经台；（演讲的）讲台；斜面高腿小桌
words.ex: The professor stood behind the lectern to deliver his speech.
words.ex_cn: 教授站在讲台后面发表演讲。
words.en: A lectern is a tall desk with a sloping top from which someone, typically a speaker or lecturer, can read while standing up.

words.ex: The professor gave a lecture on history.
words.ex_cn: 教授上了一节历史课。
words.en: A lecture is a talk that someone gives in order to teach people about a particular subject, often at a university or college.

words.ex: He speaks a local dialect in his village.
words.ex_cn: 他在村子里说一种地方方言。
words.en: A dialect is a form of a language that is spoken in a particular area and that uses some of its own words, grammar, and pronunciations.

words.ex: The new legislation bans plastic bags.
words.ex_cn: 这项新法规禁止使用塑料袋。
words.en: Legislation refers to the process of making or enacting laws by a government or other authority.

words.ex: The legislature passed a new law last week.
words.ex_cn: 立法机构上周通过了一项新法律。
words.en: A legislature is the part of a country's government that is responsible for making laws.

words.ex: The government's legitimacy depends on the people's trust.
words.ex_cn: 政府的合法性取决于人民的信任。
words.en: The quality or state of being legitimate.

words.ex: Exercise can elevate your mood.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以提升你的情绪。
words.en: To elevate something means to raise it to a higher position or level, either physically or in terms of its status or importance.

words.ex: The elevation of his skills helped him get a better job.
words.ex_cn: 他技能的提升帮助他找到了一份更好的工作。
words.en: The height to which something is elevated or to which it rises.

words.ex: He took the elevator to the 10th floor.
words.ex_cn: 他乘电梯上了十楼。
words.en: An elevator is a device that moves people or goods up and down inside a building.

words.ex: The levee held back the floodwaters, preventing a disaster.
words.ex_cn: 堤坝挡住了洪水，防止了一场灾难。
words.en: A levee is an embankment built to prevent the overflow of a river.

words.tr:
n. 轮廓；纲要；
v. 描画轮廓；概述；
words.ex: The artist drew the outline of the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家画出了山的轮廓。
words.en: An outline is a line that shows or forms the outer edge of something, or a general description or plan showing the essential features of something but not the detail.

words.ex: The company built a pipeline to carry oil.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司建造了一条输送石油的管道。
words.en: A pipeline is a long pipe, often underground, through which a liquid or gas is carried over a long distance.

words.tr: n. （报刊文章顶部的）作者署名行
words.ex: The journalist's byline was prominently displayed at the top of the article.
words.ex_cn: 记者的署名显眼地显示在文章的顶部。
words.en: A byline is a line at the head of a newspaper or magazine article giving the author's name.

words.ex: He will delineate the plan clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他将清晰地描述这个计划。
words.en: To delineate something means to describe or portray it precisely.

words.ex: The company streamlined its hiring process.
words.ex_cn: 公司简化了招聘流程。
words.en: To make something such as a business, organization, or process work more effectively by making it simpler or more efficient.

words.ex: Align your goals with your actions.
words.ex_cn: 让你的目标与行动保持一致。
words.en: To arrange something in a straight line or in the correct position in relation to something else, usually so that it is parallel to it.

words.ex: He took his words in a literal sense.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的话按字面意思理解。
words.en: If you describe something as the literal truth or a literal fact, you are emphasizing that it is true.

words.ex: He loves reading literary books.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读文学书籍。
words.en: Literary means concerned with or connected with the writing, study, or appreciation of literature.

words.tr: n. 文人；文人学士；知识界；“literatus”的复数
words.ex: The literati gathered to discuss poetry.
words.ex_cn: 文人聚集在一起讨论诗歌。
words.en: The literati are intellectuals or scholars, especially those involved in literature or the arts.

words.ex: The big black bug bit the brave boy.
words.ex_cn: 大黑虫咬了勇敢的男孩。
words.en: Alliteration is the occurrence of the same letter or sound at the beginning of adjacent or closely connected words.

words.tr:
adj. 文盲的；无知的；
n. 文盲；无知识的人；
words.ex: He is illiterate and cannot read simple signs.
words.ex_cn: 他是文盲，无法阅读简单的标识。
words.en: Someone who is illiterate cannot read or write.

words.tr: v. 消灭；毁掉；清除；抹除
words.ex: The bomb will obliterate the building.
words.ex_cn: 炸弹会摧毁那栋大楼。
words.en: To obliterate something means to remove all signs of it or to destroy it completely.

words.tr:
n. 原木；航海日志；
v. （正式地）记载；
words.ex: The fire burned brightly with a large log.
words.ex_cn: 大火用一根大原木烧得很旺。
words.en: A log is a piece of a thick branch or trunk of a tree that has been cut so that it can be used for fuel or for making things. A log is also a written record of events, often on a ship or aircraft.

words.ex: He uses logic to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他用逻辑来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Logic is a method of reasoning that involves a series of statements, each of which must be true if the statement before it is true.

words.tr: adj. 逻辑上的；合乎逻辑的；
words.ex: His argument is logical and easy to understand.
words.ex_cn: 他的论点合乎逻辑，容易理解。
words.en: In accordance with the principles of logic; reasonable.

words.ex: The company improved its logistics to deliver packages faster.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司改进了物流，以更快地配送包裹。
words.en: Logistics refers to the detailed organization and implementation of a complex operation.

words.ex: He looked at the catalog to find the book.
words.ex_cn: 他翻看目录来找那本书。
words.en: A catalog is a list of things, such as the goods you can buy from a particular company, the objects in a museum, or the books in a library.

words.ex: He gave her a sincere apology.
words.ex_cn: 他向她真诚地道歉了。
words.en: An apology is something that you say or write in order to tell someone that you are sorry that you have hurt them or caused trouble for them.

words.ex: He apologizes for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他因为迟到而道歉。
words.en: To express regret for something that one has done wrong.

words.ex: The epilogue showed what happened to the characters after the story ended.
words.ex_cn: 尾声展示了故事结束后角色们的命运。
words.en: An epilogue is a section or speech at the end of a book or play that serves as a comment on or a conclusion to what has happened.

words.ex: The two situations are analogous.
words.ex_cn: 这两种情况是相似的。
words.en: If one thing is analogous to another, the two things are similar in some way.

words.ex: The dialogue in the movie was very funny.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影中的对白非常幽默。
words.en: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people in a book, play, or film.

words.ex: He read an anthology of short stories last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚读了一本短篇故事选集。
words.en: An anthology is a collection of writings, such as poems or stories, that have been chosen by someone because they are considered to be the best or most interesting examples of their kind.

words.ex: He reads his horoscope every morning because he believes in astrology.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都看星座运势，因为他相信占星术。
words.en: Astrology is the study of the movements and relative positions of celestial bodies interpreted as having an influence on human affairs and the natural world.

words.ex: He likes biology because it teaches about animals and plants.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢生物学，因为它教关于动物和植物的知识。
words.en: Biology is the science which is concerned with the study of living things.

words.ex: He works in dermatology at the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在医院从事皮肤病学工作。
words.en: Dermatology is the branch of medicine concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of skin disorders.

words.ex: He is studying epistemology at university.
words.ex_cn: 他正在大学里学习认识论。
words.en: Epistemology is the study of the nature, sources, and limits of knowledge.

words.tr: n. 家谱学；系谱学；宗谱学；家谱（图）
words.ex: He is learning his family genealogy.
words.ex_cn: 他正在学习自己的家族家谱。
words.en: Genealogy is the study of the history of families and the line of descent from their ancestors.

words.ex: He works in meteorology and predicts the weather.
words.ex_cn: 他从事气象学工作，预测天气。
words.en: Meteorology is the scientific study of the atmosphere and of atmospheric conditions, especially as they relate to weather and weather forecasting.

words.tr: n. 神话；神话学；神话集；
words.ex: He loves reading Greek mythology.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢读希腊神话。
words.en: Mythology is a collection of myths, especially one belonging to a particular religious or cultural tradition.

words.ex: He works in neurology at the hospital.
words.ex_cn: 他在医院从事神经学工作。
words.en: The branch of medicine or biology that deals with the anatomy, functions, and organic disorders of nerves and the nervous system.

words.ex: Phenomenology is a branch of philosophy that focuses on the study of structures of experience and consciousness.
words.ex_cn: 现象学是哲学的一个分支，专注于研究经验和意识的结构。
words.en: Phenomenology is a philosophical method or approach which emphasizes the study of conscious experience as the basis for understanding the nature of reality.

words.ex: He loves zoology and studies animals in the wild.
words.ex_cn: 他热爱动物学，研究野外的动物。
words.en: Zoology is the scientific study of animals.

words.tr: adj. 话多的；健谈的；喋喋不休的
words.ex: He is a loquacious man who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个整天喋喋不休的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as loquacious, you mean that they talk a lot.

words.ex: He uses colloquial words when talking with friends.
words.ex_cn: 他和朋友聊天时使用口语化的词语。
words.en: Colloquial language is informal language that is used in ordinary conversation rather than in writing or formal speech.

words.tr: adj. 雄辩的；有口才的；有说服力的
words.ex: He gave an eloquent speech at the ceremony.
words.ex_cn: 他在仪式上发表了富有感染力的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone as eloquent, you mean that they are able to express their ideas and opinions well, so that other people understand them and are influenced by them.

words.tr: adj. 词藻浮华的；夸大的；做作的
words.ex: He gave a grandiloquent speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's language as grandiloquent, you mean that it is extremely formal, elaborate, or exaggerated, and is used to impress people.

words.ex: He spoke a soliloquy alone on stage.
words.ex_cn: 他独自在舞台上说了一段独白。
words.en: A soliloquy is a speech in a play in which a character speaks their thoughts aloud, often when they are alone on stage.

words.ex: The teacher gave a lucid explanation of the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师对这道数学题做了一个易懂的解释。
words.en: If someone is lucid, they are able to understand things clearly and think clearly, especially when they have been very ill or confused.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；易懂的
words.ex: The water in the mountain stream was so pellucid that we could see the fish swimming.
words.ex_cn: 山间溪流中的水如此清澈，我们可以看到鱼儿在游动。
words.en: If something is pellucid, it is very clear and easy to understand.

words.ex: The teacher elucidated the math problem with a simple diagram.
words.ex_cn: 老师用一个简单的图表阐明了这道数学题。
words.en: To make something clear or easy to understand by explaining or giving reasons.

words.ex: The glass is translucent, so you can see light through it.
words.ex_cn: 这种玻璃是半透明的，所以你能看到光透过它。
words.en: If a material or substance is translucent, it is almost transparent, allowing some light to pass through it but not detailed shapes.

words.tr: v. 暗指；（间接）提到；影射
words.ex: He alluded to the problem without naming it.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示了这个问题，但没有点明。
words.en: To allude to something means to mention it in an indirect way.

words.ex: They collude to cheat in the exam.
words.ex_cn: 他们串通在考试中作弊。
words.en: If one person colludes with another, they co-operate with them secretly or illegally.

words.ex: He deluded himself into thinking he would win.
words.ex_cn: 他欺骗自己，以为自己会赢。
words.en: If you delude yourself, you let yourself believe that something is true, even though it is not true.

words.ex: The tricky question eluded even the best students.
words.ex_cn: 这道难题难倒了即使是最优秀的学生。
words.en: If something that you want eludes you, you fail to obtain it. If you elude someone or something, you avoid them or escape from them.

words.tr: adj. 难以捉摸的；不易被抓获（觉察、理解或记忆）的；
words.ex: The truth remained elusive.
words.ex_cn: 真相难以捉摸。
words.en: Difficult to find, catch, or achieve; difficult to remember or understand.

words.ex: The quiet music was a prelude to the loud concert.
words.ex_cn: 轻柔的音乐是盛大音乐会的前奏。
words.en: A prelude is an introductory piece of music, event, or action that comes before a more important one.

words.ex: The leaf occluded the pipe.
words.ex_cn: 叶子堵住了管道。
words.en: To occlude means to block or stop up a passage, opening, or vessel.

words.ex: The mirror creates an illusion of a bigger room.
words.ex_cn: 镜子制造出房间更大的错觉。
words.en: An illusion is a false idea or belief, especially about yourself or your situation.

words.tr: n. 魔术师；爱幻想的人；幻觉论者；幻觉派的艺术家
words.ex: The illusionist performed a series of mind-bending tricks.
words.ex_cn: 这位魔术师表演了一系列令人费解的魔术。
words.en: An illusionist is a person who performs tricks that deceive the eye or the mind, especially a magician.

words.tr: adj. 可笑的；荒谬的；滑稽的
words.ex: It is ludicrous to wear a coat in summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天穿外套真是荒谬。
words.en: If you describe something as ludicrous, you are emphasizing that you think it is foolish, unreasonable, or unsuitable.

words.tr:
adj. 笨拙的；不机敏的；笨手笨脚的
n. 一个笨拙愚蠢的人
words.ex: He was maladroit when he dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: If you describe someone as maladroit, you mean that they are clumsy or awkward, especially in social situations.

words.tr: n. 身体不适；不快；萎靡不振；痼疾
words.ex: She felt a general malaise after the long flight.
words.ex_cn: 长途飞行后，她感到全身不适。
words.en: A general feeling of discomfort, illness, or unease whose exact cause is difficult to identify.

words.tr: n. 荒唐的用词错误；被误用的词
words.ex: He said 'a wise man' instead of 'a whale of a man'—that was a malapropism.
words.ex_cn: 他说了‘a wise man’而不是‘a whale of a man’——那就是一个用词不当。
words.en: The mistaken use of a word in place of a similar-sounding one, often with unintentionally amusing effect, as in 'dance a flamingo' (instead of flamenco).

words.ex: The malevolent wizard cast a dark spell.
words.ex_cn: 那个有恶意的巫师施了一个黑暗咒语。
words.en: Having or showing a wish to harm others; malicious.

words.ex: He sent a malicious email to hurt his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他发了一封怀恶意的邮件来伤害他的朋友。
words.en: If you describe someone's words or actions as malicious, you mean that they are intended to harm people or their reputation, or to cause them embarrassment and upset.

words.tr:
adj. 有害的；恶意的
v. 中伤；污蔑
words.ex: The virus is malign and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒是有害的，并且传播迅速。
words.en: If you malign someone, you say unpleasant and untrue things about them. If something is malign, it is harmful or evil.

words.tr:
adj. 手工的；体力的；
n. 说明书；
words.ex: He made a manual copy of the letter.
words.ex_cn: 他手工抄写了一封信。
words.en: A manual is a book which tells you how to do something or how a piece of machinery works.

words.ex: The king decided to manumit all the slaves.
words.ex_cn: 国王决定解放所有奴隶。
words.en: To release from slavery or bondage; set free.

words.tr:
n. 制造；
v. （用机器大量）制造；虚构；捏造；
words.ex: The manufacture of cars needs many workers.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的制造需要很多工人。
words.en: To manufacture something means to make it in a factory, usually in large quantities.

words.ex: The law will emancipate slaves.
words.ex_cn: 法律将解放奴隶。
words.en: To emancipate someone means to set them free from something that restricts their freedom to do what they want.

words.ex: He tried to manipulate the results to win the game.
words.ex_cn: 他试图操纵结果来赢得比赛。
words.en: To manipulate something means to handle or control it skillfully, often in a way that is considered unfair or dishonest.

words.tr:
n. 授权；任期；委任；命令
v. 授权；委任
words.ex: The government has a mandate from the people to change the law.
words.ex_cn: 政府得到了人民的授权来修改法律。
words.en: If someone is given a mandate to carry out a particular policy or task, they are given the official authority to do it.

words.tr: adj. 强制的；法定的；义务的；
words.ex: Wearing a helmet is mandatory for cyclists.
words.ex_cn: 骑自行车时戴头盔是强制的。
words.en: If something is mandatory, it is required by law or by a rule or regulation.

words.tr:
n. 指挥；命令；
v. 掌握；
words.ex: The general has command of the army.
words.ex_cn: 将军指挥着军队。
words.en: If someone in authority commands you to do something, they tell you that you must do it.

words.tr:
n. （下反对命令）取消（前一命令）；调回；取消（定货）
v. （下反对命令）取消（前一命令）；调回；取消（定货）
words.ex: The general countermanded the order to attack.
words.ex_cn: 将军取消了进攻的命令。
words.en: If you countermand an order, you cancel it, usually by giving a different order.

words.tr: adj. 要求高的；费力的； v. 需要；“demand”的现在分词；
words.ex: The job is demanding because it needs long hours and high focus.
words.ex_cn: 这份工作要求高，因为它需要长时间工作和高度专注。
words.en: Requiring much effort or attention; exacting.

words.tr:
n. 申斥；谴责
v. 斥责；训斥
words.ex: The teacher gave him a reprimand for talking in class.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他上课讲话而训斥了他。
words.en: A reprimand is a formal or official expression of disapproval, typically by a person in authority.

words.ex: The hallmark of a good teacher is patience.
words.ex_cn: 好老师的标志是耐心。
words.en: A hallmark is a distinctive characteristic or attribute that is typical of a particular person or thing.

words.ex: The invention of the wheel was a landmark in human history.
words.ex_cn: 轮子的发明是人类历史上的一个里程碑。
words.en: A landmark is a building or feature of a landscape that is easily seen and recognized from a distance, especially one that enables someone to establish their location.

words.ex: The company has a famous trademark on its logo.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司在其标志上有一个著名的标记。
words.en: A trademark is a recognizable sign, design, or expression which identifies products or services of a particular source from those of others.

words.tr: adj. 不同寻常的；非凡的；显著的；值得注意的；
words.ex: She made a remarkable improvement in just one month.
words.ex_cn: 她在短短一个月内取得了不同寻常的进步。
words.en: Unusual or striking in a way that attracts attention.

words.ex: The climax of the movie was a big chase scene.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影的高潮是一场大追捕场景。
words.en: The climax is the most exciting or important part of a play, film, or piece of music, which usually happens near the end.

words.tr: n. 突降；苍白无力的结尾；令人扫兴的结尾
words.ex: The movie ended with an anticlimax.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影以一个平淡的结局收尾。
words.en: An anticlimax is a disappointing end to an exciting or impressive series of events.

words.ex: He achieved maximal efficiency with minimal effort.
words.ex_cn: 他以最小的努力达到了最大的效率。
words.en: Maximal means the greatest or highest possible in degree or amount.

words.tr: n. 巨头；大亨；大资本家
words.ex: The magnate owns many hotels and airlines.
words.ex_cn: 这位大亨拥有许多酒店和航空公司。
words.en: A magnate is a person who is very rich and powerful, especially in a particular industry.

words.tr: adj. 宽宏大量的；有雅量的
words.ex: He was magnanimous and forgave his enemy.
words.ex_cn: 他宽宏大量，原谅了他的敌人。
words.en: If you are magnanimous, you behave kindly and generously toward someone, especially after defeating them or being treated badly by them.

words.ex: The microscope can magnify small objects.
words.ex_cn: 显微镜可以放大微小的物体。
words.en: To magnify something means to make it appear larger than it is, especially by using a lens or microscope. It can also mean to exaggerate or make something seem more important or serious than it really is.

words.ex: They placed a memorial at the site of the accident.
words.ex_cn: 他们在事故地点放置了一座纪念物。
words.en: A memorial is a structure or event established to remind people of a person or event.

words.ex: This custom has existed from time immemorial.
words.ex_cn: 这个习俗从远古时代就存在了。
words.en: Something that is immemorial has existed or been happening for such a long time that it cannot be remembered.

words.tr: adj. 值得纪念的；难忘的；
words.ex: That vacation was a memorable trip.
words.ex_cn: 那次旅行是一次值得纪念的旅程。
words.en: Something that is memorable is worth remembering or likely to be remembered, because it is special or very enjoyable.

words.ex: They plant trees to commemorate the fallen soldiers.
words.ex_cn: 他们种树以纪念阵亡的士兵。
words.en: To commemorate an important event or person means to remember them by means of a special action, ceremony, or specially created object.

words.ex: He uses mnemonics to remember the dates.
words.ex_cn: 他使用助记法来记住这些日期。
words.en: Mnemonics is a method or system for improving the memory by using formulas or techniques.

words.tr:
v. 评论；表达意见；
n. 评论；意见；
words.ex: He commented on the movie last night.
words.ex_cn: 他昨晚对这部电影发表了评论。
words.en: A comment is something that you say which expresses your opinion of something or which gives an explanation of it.

words.tr: n. 解说词；评论；实况报道；
words.ex: The commentator gave live commentary during the soccer match.
words.ex_cn: 解说员在足球比赛期间进行了现场解说。
words.en: A commentary is a spoken or written description of an event or situation that is broadcast or published as it occurs.

words.ex: My mentor helped me choose my career path.
words.ex_cn: 我的导师帮助我选择了职业道路。
words.en: A mentor is a person who gives a younger or less experienced person help and advice over a period of time, especially at work or school.

words.tr:
adj. 贸易的；商业的；
n. 广告；
words.ex: The commercial ship sailed to another country.
words.ex_cn: 这艘贸易船只驶向了另一个国家。
words.en: Commercial relates to the business of buying and selling goods and services.

words.ex: The merchant sells fresh fruit every morning.
words.ex_cn: 商人每天早上卖新鲜水果。
words.en: A merchant is a person who buys and sells goods, especially one who owns a shop.

words.ex: He runs a mercantile shop in the old town.
words.ex_cn: 他在老城区经营一家商业店铺。
words.en: relating to trade or commerce; commercial.

words.tr:
adj. 唯利是图的；雇佣的
n. 雇佣兵；唯利是图者
words.ex: He works as a mercenary for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱当雇佣兵。
words.en: A mercenary is a professional soldier hired to serve in a foreign army.

words.ex: The store sells cheap merchandise.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店出售廉价商品。
words.en: Goods to be bought and sold.

words.ex: A bird emerged from the trees.
words.ex_cn: 一只鸟从树中浮现出来。
words.en: If something or someone emerges, they come out of or move out of something and become visible.

words.ex: He called an emergency doctor when he felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 当他感到不舒服时，他叫了急诊医生。
words.en: An emergency is an unexpected and usually dangerous situation that calls for immediate action.

words.ex: The diver submerge to explore the coral reef.
words.ex_cn: 潜水员潜水去探索珊瑚礁。
words.en: To submerge something means to put it below the surface of a liquid, especially water. If something submerges, it goes below the surface of a liquid.

words.ex: He immersed the cloth in water.
words.ex_cn: 他把布浸在水里。
words.en: To immerse something or someone means to put them into a liquid so that they are completely covered by it. It can also mean to involve oneself deeply in a particular activity or interest.

words.ex: The fence marks the perimeter of the garden.
words.ex_cn: 围栏标出了花园的边界。
words.en: The perimeter of an area or object is the total length of its sides or outer boundary.

words.ex: The school is five kilometers from my house.
words.ex_cn: 学校离我家五公里。
words.en: A kilometer is a unit of length in the metric system, equal to one thousand meters.

words.ex: The car's odometer shows 50,000 miles.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车的里程表显示50,000英里。
words.en: An odometer is an instrument in a vehicle that measures and displays the total distance that the vehicle has traveled.

words.ex: He checked the thermometer to see the temperature.
words.ex_cn: 他看了温度计来查看温度。
words.en: A thermometer is an instrument for measuring and indicating temperature.

words.ex: The diameter of the circle is 10 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个圆的直径是10厘米。
words.en: A straight line passing from side to side through the center of a body or figure, especially a circle or sphere.

words.ex: The butterfly has perfect symmetry.
words.ex_cn: 这只蝴蝶有完美的对称性。
words.en: Symmetry is the quality of being made up of exactly similar parts facing each other or around an axis.

words.ex: The design of the building is perfectly symmetric.
words.ex_cn: 这座建筑的设计非常对称。
words.en: Something that is symmetric has sides that are equal in size and shape or are arranged in a balanced way.

words.tr: adj. 不对称的；不均匀的
words.ex: The two sides of the box are asymmetric.
words.ex_cn: 盒子的两边不对称。
words.en: An asymmetric object does not have the same shape, size, or arrangement on both sides of a central line.

words.ex: The dimension of the box is 10 cm by 5 cm.
words.ex_cn: 这个盒子的尺寸是10厘米乘5厘米。
words.en: A dimension is a measurement of something in a particular direction, or the scope or scale of something.

words.ex: His salary is commensurate with his experience.
words.ex_cn: 他的薪水与他的经验相称。
words.en: If the level of one thing is commensurate with another, the first level is in proportion to the second.

words.ex: The microbe causes sickness.
words.ex_cn: 这种微生物会引起疾病。
words.en: A microbe is a very small living thing, which you can only see if you use a microscope. Some microbes can cause diseases.

words.ex: A microorganism can cause sickness.
words.ex_cn: 微生物会导致疾病。
words.en: A microorganism is a very small living thing that you can only see with a microscope.

words.ex: He spoke into the microphone to be heard clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他对着麦克风说话，以便被清楚地听到。
words.en: A microphone is a device that is used to make sounds louder or to record them.

words.ex: He looks at the bug through a microscope.
words.ex_cn: 他通过显微镜观察这只虫子。
words.en: An instrument used for viewing objects that are too small to be seen by the naked eye, especially one that uses a combination of lenses to produce a magnified image.

words.ex: He performed a mime on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他在街上表演了哑剧。
words.en: A mime is a form of performance art where the performer uses gestures and movements without speech to convey a story or emotion. As a verb, to mime means to imitate or mimic actions or expressions without using words.

words.tr:
n. 哑剧；（英）圣诞童话剧
v. 打手势；演哑剧
words.ex: The children laughed at the clown's pantomime.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们笑了，因为小丑的哑剧表演。
words.en: Pantomime is a type of entertainment where performers express a story or represent characters through gestures and body movements without using speech.

words.ex: The child mimics her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If someone or something mimics another person or thing, they try to be like them or copy their behavior or characteristics.

words.ex: The bird uses mimicry to copy other animals' sounds.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟通过模仿来复制其他动物的声音。
words.en: The action or art of imitating someone or something, especially in order to entertain or ridicule.

words.ex: The child imitates her mother's voice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子模仿她妈妈的声音。
words.en: If you imitate someone, you copy what they do or produce.

words.tr: adj. 无法仿效的；不可比拟的
words.ex: Her inimitable style of writing has captured the hearts of many readers.
words.ex_cn: 她那独特的写作风格赢得了许多读者的心。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as inimitable, you mean that they are so good or unusual that it is unlikely that anyone or anything else could be like them.

words.ex: He is an eminent scientist who won the Nobel Prize.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位获得诺贝尔奖的杰出科学家。
words.en: An eminent person is well-known and respected, especially because they are good at their profession.

words.tr: adj. 即将发生的；临近的；
words.ex: An imminent storm is coming soon.
words.ex_cn: 一场即将发生的风暴很快就要来了。
words.en: If you say that something is imminent, especially something unpleasant, you mean it is almost certain to happen very soon.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.tr: adj. 杰出的；卓越的；出类拔萃的
words.ex: He is a pre-eminent scientist in his field.
words.ex_cn: 他是该领域最杰出的科学家。
words.en: If someone or something is pre-eminent in a group, they are more important, powerful, or capable than other people or things in the group.

words.ex: The noise will diminish after midnight.
words.ex_cn: 午夜后噪音会减少。
words.en: If something diminishes, or if something diminishes it, it becomes reduced in size, importance, or intensity.

words.tr: adj. 最低限度的；极少的；最小的；
words.ex: He made minimal changes to the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对计划做了最低限度的修改。
words.en: Something that is minimal is very small in quantity, value, or degree.

words.tr: v. 减到最少；使最小化；
words.ex: Try to minimize waste in the kitchen.
words.ex_cn: 尽量减少厨房里的浪费。
words.en: To minimize something means to reduce it to the smallest possible amount or degree.

words.ex: The minority group voted for change.
words.ex_cn: 少数群体投票支持变革。
words.en: A minority is a group of people within a community or country who are different from the majority of the people there in race, religion, or political beliefs.

words.ex: The minuscule dot was hard to see with the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 那个极小的点用肉眼很难看到。
words.en: If you describe something as minuscule, you mean that it is very small.

words.ex: He was obsessed with the minutiae of daily life.
words.ex_cn: 他对日常生活的琐事着迷。
words.en: The small, precise, or trivial details of something.

words.tr:
adj. 极小的；特小的；微小的
n. 小的人；指小词缀；爱称
words.ex: The diminutive cat sat on the small mat.
words.ex_cn: 那只小巧的猫坐在小垫子上。
words.en: A diminutive person or object is very small.

words.tr:
adj. 微型的；
n. 微型画；小型模型；
words.ex: He bought a miniature car for his collection.
words.ex_cn: 他为他的收藏买了一辆微型汽车。
words.en: A miniature is a very small detailed painting, often a portrait. It can also refer to a small-scale model or representation of something.

words.ex: The boy was punished for his misdeed.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因他的恶劣行为而受到惩罚。
words.en: A misdeed is a wrong or illegal deed; a crime or sin.

words.tr: n. 轻罪；品行不端；轻刑罪
words.ex: He committed a misdemeanor by parking illegally.
words.ex_cn: 他因非法停车而犯下轻罪。
words.en: A misdemeanor is a less serious crime than a felony, punishable by less than a year of imprisonment.

words.tr: v. 行为不端；行为无礼貌
words.ex: The boy misbehaved in class.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩在课堂上行为不端。
words.en: If someone, especially a child, misbehaves, they behave in a way that is not acceptable to other people.

words.ex: The miscreant was caught red-handed.
words.ex_cn: 那个恶棍被当场抓住。
words.en: A miscreant is someone who behaves badly or does not obey the law.

words.ex: She wears modish clothes every day.
words.ex_cn: 她每天穿时髦的衣服。
words.en: If something is modish, it is fashionable and modern.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；老式的； v. “outmode”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: This phone is outmoded and needs to be replaced.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，需要更换。
words.en: If you describe something as outmoded, you mean that you think it is old-fashioned and no longer useful or relevant to modern life.

words.ex: They will remodel their kitchen next month.
words.ex_cn: 他们下个月要重新装修厨房。
words.en: To remodel something means to change its structure or form, often to improve it.

words.ex: He will modify the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会更改计划。
words.en: To change something slightly, especially in order to make it more suitable for a particular purpose.

words.tr: adj. 不多的；适度的；谦虚的；
words.ex: He made a modest profit last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年的利润不多。
words.en: If you say that someone is modest, you approve of them because they do not talk much about their abilities or achievements.

words.ex: He wears a monocle to read books.
words.ex_cn: 他戴单片眼镜看书。
words.en: A monocle is a type of corrective lens used to correct or enhance the vision in only one eye.

words.tr: n. 独白；独角戏；长篇大论
words.ex: He gave a monologue on stage.
words.ex_cn: 他在舞台上发表了一段独白。
words.en: A monologue is a long speech by one person, especially in a play or film, or a long speech by one person during a conversation.

words.ex: He has a monopoly on selling ice cream in this town.
words.ex_cn: 他在这座小镇上垄断了冰淇淋的销售。
words.en: If a company, person, or state has a monopoly on something such as an industry, they have complete control over it, so that it is impossible for others to become involved in it.

words.tr: n. 单调；枯燥；千篇一律
words.ex: He felt bored because of the monotony of his daily work.
words.ex_cn: 他因为日常工作的单调而感到无聊。
words.en: If you refer to the monotony of something, you are criticizing it because it is boring and has no variety.

words.tr: adj.  独块巨石的；整体的；庞大的；单一的；统一的
words.ex: The ancient temple was built from a monolithic stone.
words.ex_cn: 这座古代神庙是由一块巨石建成的。
words.en: A monolithic structure is extremely large and made of one piece or one type of material.

words.ex: The manager decided to demote him for poor performance.
words.ex_cn: 经理因他表现不佳决定降职他。
words.en: If someone is demoted, they are given a lower rank or a less important position than they had before.

words.tr: v. 促进；推动；宣传；推销；
words.ex: Exercise can promote good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进健康。
words.en: To promote means to help something to happen, develop, or increase, or to raise someone to a higher position or rank.

words.tr:
adj. 偏远的；久远的；
n. 遥控器；
words.ex: The village is in a remote area far from the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于远离城市的偏远地区。
words.en: Remote areas are far away from cities and places where most people live, and are therefore difficult to get to.

words.ex: The children caused a big commotion in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在教室里制造了很大的喧闹。
words.en: A commotion is a lot of noise, confusion, and excitement.

words.ex: The bacteria show high motility in warm water.
words.ex_cn: 这种细菌在温水中具有很高的运动能力。
words.en: The ability of an organism or fluid to move or be moved.

words.ex: His motive was to help his family.
words.ex_cn: 他的动机是帮助家人。
words.en: Your motive for doing something is your reason for doing it.

words.ex: The locomotive pulled the train down the track.
words.ex_cn: 机车拉着火车沿着轨道行驶。
words.en: A locomotive is a powered rail vehicle used for pulling trains.

words.ex: Good teachers motivate students to learn.
words.ex_cn: 好老师激励学生学习。
words.en: To motivate someone means to provide them with a reason for doing something, especially something that requires effort.

words.ex: They will nominate her for the award.
words.ex_cn: 他们将提名她获得这个奖项。
words.en: If someone is nominated for a job or position, their name is formally suggested as a candidate for it.

words.ex: He accepted a nominal fee for the service.
words.ex_cn: 他为这项服务收取了微不足道的费用。
words.en: If you say that something is nominal, you mean that it is very small in comparison to the real value or importance of something.

words.ex: The committee decided to denominate the new park 'Green Haven.'
words.ex_cn: 委员会决定将新公园命名为'绿洲'。
words.en: To give a name to something or someone, often in a formal or official way.

words.tr: adj. 耻辱的；不名誉的；不光彩的
words.ex: He faced an ignominious defeat in the election.
words.ex_cn: 他在选举中遭遇了耻辱的失败。
words.en: If you describe an experience or action as ignominious, you mean it is embarrassing because it shows a great lack of success.

words.ex: His temperature is normal.
words.ex_cn: 他的体温正常。
words.en: Something that is normal is usual and ordinary, and is what people expect.

words.ex: The teacher did normalization of the test scores.
words.ex_cn: 老师对考试成绩进行了正常化。
words.en: The process of making something normal or standard, especially in the context of social or political relations.

words.ex: The boy has an abnormal heartbeat.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩的心跳不正常。
words.en: Deviating from what is normal or usual, typically in a way that is undesirable or worrying.

words.tr: adj. 偏离规则的；反常的
words.ex: The temperature was anomalous for this season.
words.ex_cn: 这个季节的温度异常。
words.en: Deviating from what is standard, normal, or expected.

words.ex: The enormity of the crime shocked the whole city.
words.ex_cn: 这桩罪行的极恶震惊了整个城市。
words.en: If you refer to the enormity of something that you consider to be a problem or difficulty, you are referring to its very great size, extent, or seriousness.

words.ex: The teacher will announce the results tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 老师明天将宣布结果。
words.en: To announce something means to make it known publicly or officially.

words.ex: Can you pronounce this word correctly?
words.ex_cn: 你能正确发音这个词吗？
words.en: To pronounce means to make the sound of a word or letter with your voice. It can also mean to declare or announce something officially or formally.

words.tr: v. 发音；宣告；“pronounce”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 显著的；
words.ex: He pronounced the word correctly.
words.ex_cn: 他正确地发音了这个单词。
words.en: Something that is pronounced is very noticeable or obvious.

words.tr: v. 公开指责；告发；揭发
words.ex: He denounces corruption in his speech.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲中谴责腐败。
words.en: If you denounce a person or an action, you criticize them severely and publicly because you feel strongly that they are wrong or evil.

words.tr: v. 声明放弃；与...断绝关系
words.ex: He renounced his citizenship last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年放弃了国籍。
words.en: If you renounce a belief or a way of behaving, you say and show that you no longer hold that belief or will behave in that way.

words.tr: v. （清楚地）发音；清楚地表明；阐明
words.ex: He tries to enunciate each word clearly.
words.ex_cn: 他努力清晰地发出每个单词的音。
words.en: To enunciate means to pronounce words clearly and distinctly, or to state something clearly and in detail.

words.ex: He uses a fake name for anonymity.
words.ex_cn: 他用假名来保持匿名。
words.en: The condition of being anonymous; the state of not having one's name or identity known.

words.ex: Happy is synonymous with joyful.
words.ex_cn: 快乐与喜悦是同义的。
words.en: If you say that one thing is synonymous with another, you mean that the two things are very closely associated with each other so that one suggests the other or one cannot exist without the other.

words.ex: He writes books under a pseudonym.
words.ex_cn: 他用笔名写书。
words.en: A pseudonym is a name that someone, especially a writer, uses instead of their real name.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.tr: adj. 迷失方向的； v. “disorient”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He felt disoriented after the power went out.
words.ex_cn: 停电后他感到迷失方向。
words.en: If you are disoriented, you have lost your sense of direction, or you feel confused and not sure where you are or what you should do.

words.ex: The origin of this tradition is unknown.
words.ex_cn: 这个传统的起源不明。
words.en: The origin of something is the point or place where it begins, or the cause from which it arises.

words.tr:
adj. 原来的；有创造性的；原版的；新颖的；
n. 原件；原稿；
words.ex: This is the original book I bought last year.
words.ex_cn: 这是我去年买的那本原版书。
words.en: An original piece of writing or music was written recently and has not been published or performed before.

words.ex: This tradition originates from ancient times.
words.ex_cn: 这个传统起源于古代。
words.en: To originate means to have a specific beginning or to start something.

words.tr: n. 被排斥者；被抛弃者；
words.ex: He became an outcast after speaking the truth.
words.ex_cn: 他因为说出真相而被排斥。
words.en: An outcast is someone who is not accepted by a group of people or by society.

words.tr: n. 路由；路径选择；（材料或产品的）加工路线安排
words.ex: The router uses routing to send data to the right place.
words.ex_cn: 路由器使用路由将数据发送到正确的地方。
words.en: Routing refers to the process of selecting paths in a network along which to send network traffic, or the act of directing or sending something along a particular path.

words.tr: adj. 外向的；即将离职的；往外去的；
words.ex: He is an outgoing boy who loves talking to new people.
words.ex_cn: 他是个外向的男孩，喜欢和新朋友聊天。
words.en: Someone who is outgoing is very friendly and likes meeting and talking to people.

words.ex: They live on the outskirts of the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在城市的郊区。
words.en: The outskirts of a city or town are the parts of it that are farthest away from its center.

words.ex: He wore an outlandish hat to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他戴了一顶奇异的帽子去参加派对。
words.en: If you describe something as outlandish, you mean that it is very unusual, strange, or exaggerated.

words.tr: n. 出口；发泄途径；经销店；折扣店
words.ex: The river flows out through an outlet.
words.ex_cn: 河水通过一个出口流出。
words.en: An outlet is a hole or pipe through which liquid or air can flow out, or a point in a wall where you can connect electrical equipment to the electricity supply.

words.ex: The general managed to outmaneuver the enemy forces.
words.ex_cn: 这位将军设法用计谋胜过了敌军。
words.en: To outmaneuver someone means to use clever tactics to gain an advantage over them, especially in a military context or in any kind of strategic competition.

words.ex: He overcame his fear of speaking in public.
words.ex_cn: 他克服了当众演讲的恐惧。
words.en: If you overcome a problem or a feeling, you successfully deal with it and control it.

words.tr:
n. 彻底检修；大修；彻底革新；全面修订
v. 彻底检修；超过（赛跑对手）
words.ex: The plane needs an overhaul before the next flight.
words.ex_cn: 这架飞机在下次飞行前需要彻底检修。
words.en: If you overhaul a system or method, you examine it carefully and make many changes in it in order to improve it.

words.tr:
v. 推翻；颠覆；打倒
n. 推翻；颠覆；打倒
words.ex: The court will overturn the old law.
words.ex_cn: 法院将推翻这项旧法律。
words.en: If a decision, result, etc. is overturned, it is officially changed so that it becomes the opposite of what it was before.

words.tr: v. 使不知所措；使无法解决；击败；压垮；淹没
words.ex: The homework overwhelms her every night.
words.ex_cn: 每天晚上的作业让她感到不堪重负。
words.en: To overwhelm means to bury or drown beneath a huge mass of something, or to defeat someone completely.

words.ex: His overbearing boss always tells him what to do.
words.ex_cn: 他专横的老板总是告诉他该做什么。
words.en: If you describe someone as overbearing, you mean that they behave in a very unpleasant way because they are too confident of their own importance.

words.ex: He overlooked the mistake in the report.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了报告中的错误。
words.en: If you overlook a fact or problem, you do not notice it, or do not realize how important it is.

words.tr: v. 伸得过长；做得过火；走过头
words.ex: He overreachs his authority and makes bad decisions.
words.ex_cn: 他越权行事，做出了错误的决定。
words.en: If you say that someone overreaches themselves, you mean that they fail at something because they are trying to do more than they are able to.

words.tr: adj. 过分劳累的；过度兴奋的；过分紧张的
words.ex: He felt overwrought after working 16 hours straight.
words.ex_cn: 他连续工作了16个小时，感到精疲力尽。
words.en: If someone is overwrought, they are very upset and are not thinking or behaving calmly or sensibly.
